front.title: MAP: Family Index and Submission Overview

abstract.t: The Manolito Agent Protocol (MAP) is a family of specifications for a decentralized, permissionless network of autonomous AI agents. MAP evolves the capability-oriented spirit of the historical Manolito (MP2P) file-sharing network into a modern agent fabric in which participants advertise what they can do — models, tools, memory domains, compute — and requesters route work by semantic capability, verifiable evidence of past behavior, price, and locally measured performance. This document is the cover/index for the MAP family: it lists the companion documents, states the reading order, and records the submission status. Each companion document carries its own normative text; this index defines no wire format, code point, or protocol behavior.

section.name: Family overview
section.t: MAP is written as a set of focused Internet-Drafts rather than one monolith, so each concern (identity, transport, discovery, tasks, trust, payments, operations) can advance and be reviewed independently while sharing one envelope, one identity model, and one registry index. They were written for the IETF Independent Stream; see SUBMISSION.md for why that stream cannot host the family's registries and what the publication path is now. section.name: Submission status
section.t: The family was written for the IETF Independent Stream (each draft's submissiontype: independent front-matter records this). That stream cannot create the ~20 IANA registries this family defines, nor grant the registration policies they use (RFC 8726 §2/§4/§5), so the family's registries are stewarded outside the RFC series per draft-map-ops-01 §3.5 and only narrow, registry-free extracts are submitted. SUBMISSION.md records the current plan.

Both reference implementations (map-rs, map-go) pass the full test-vector set and the live pairwise interop matrix (26/26 — 16 core, 6 task, 4 pay), which meets draft-map-ops-01 §6.1 mechanically; both are the work of one author, so the independence criterion is not met substantively. The documents remain in draft pending human/expert review.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: This document is a family index and defines no protocol mechanisms of its own; it therefore introduces no new security considerations. MAP's security model is normative in the protocol documents: draft-map-core-01 (envelope integrity, session channel binding, anti-replay), draft-map-identity-01 (agent identity and delegation attenuation), draft-map-trust-01 (receipt-based, self-reported-trust-free reputation), and draft-map-pay-01 (settlement evidence and disputes). draft-map-arch-01 states the family threat model.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document requests no IANA actions. The consolidated registry index for the family is draft-map-wire-01; individual registries are defined and populated by the protocol documents.
